snippets.text: This video is sponsored by Laggerfast
GamingVPN. Stay until the end to learn
more. Hey, welcome back. With the global
release being right around the corner, I
figured it was time to release an
updated version of this guide. Given the
uncertainty of the global server
settings, I will be covering each topic
in a broad way, mentioning if any
specific part of any specific system was
added in a later season if we have no
confirmations of them being present in
the global version. For this reason,
each topic will not go into excruciating
details, rather providing an overview of
what each system and content does and
provides. For gearing and progression
focused topics, I will put a link in the
description below to my building guides
for a more in-depth look at them. And
for specific dungeon guides, I will be
linking a playlist with all of my
dungeon and raid guides as well. As for
more class specific skill and macro
setups, you will be able to find those
in the resource channels on my Discord,
also linked in the description below.
With that out of the way, let's get into
it. First, daily duties. These are the
only daily type piece of content in the
game and can be accessed in your journal
under the duty tab. Duties will require
you to slay monsters and bosses in your
faction's open field and will award you
with kina as well as uncapped AP upon
completion as well as random bonus
rewards with the most notable rewards
being soul crystals and cube keys.
Duties allowances are server based. Next
are weekly contracts. These are almost
identical to duties in form with the
main difference being that they are
purchased at command merchants with the
shop replenishing on a weekly basis.
Once the contract is acquired, you can
click on them in your inventory to
reward the quest and rewards. Notable
rewards also include soul crystals and
keys, but also feature AP instead of
kina in the bonus rewards, as well as
amplification stone fragments and board
fragments. Can also purchase command
contracts for merchants within the
abyss. With these requiring to kill
monsters within the given abyss zone for
the basic contracts and slaying players
of the opposite camp within the area,
but the special contracts added in
chapter one. The regular contracts will
award you with abyss points, abyssal
power shards, amplification stone
fragments, cube keys, unstable stinger
shards, as well as asphel board
fragments. And the special contract also
provide medals. Contracts allowances are
server based, meaning you will only be
running them on a single character. Next
are seal dungeons. These are mini
dungeons that can be found all over the
faction specific open field. Once you
venture inside, you will be asked to
complete a wide variety of tasks from
clearing the dungeon or its monsters to
defeating a boss or even completing a
tile memory miniame. Upon completion,
these will award a Davian board
crystals, kina enhancement stones,
pantheon statue fragments, and feather
down for special wings, and will also
provide a bit of AP for completing
dungeons on the opposite factions map.
Due to these providing divin crystals,
you will want to complete every single
one of them as part of your initial
character progression, including the one
present on the opposite faction's map.
Seal dungeon progression is character
based. Next, stronghold. These are
similar to seal dungeons, but instead
awarding upgrade material for your
build, as well as some kina and mana
stones. Due to the belt upgrades and
domination events, you will also want to
complete every single one on both
factions map eventually, although at a
lower priority than seal dungeons.
Stronghold's progression is character
based. Next, kibilisks. These act as
quick travel points as well as
resurrection points. In the overworld,
approaching one will unlock it, enabling
you to teleport to them as well as
resurrect to them if you die within
their vicinity. In dungeons, they
similarly act as teleport points and
resurrection locations, but will require
to be interacted with to unlock and will
have to be unlocked again every time you
reenter the dungeon. Another type of
kibelisks are kisks, which are basically
portable kibelisks. You can purchase
these from merchants, then set them down
in eligible areas to resurrect in case
of death. These are mostly utilized in
PvP scenarios like rifting and large
scale PVP events. Next, monolith.
Monoliths can be found in your faction's
main hub on each map, both on the
faction maps and in the abyss.
Increasing their levels required to feed
them feathers that can be gathered in
the same map as the monolith. Increasing
a monolith's level will provide you with
skill points, PVE amulet enhancement
material, cube keys, soul codexes,
skins, and titles for the faction map
monolith, and asphel crystals, PvP
amulet enhancement material,
amplification stone fragments, skins,
titles, and PvP permanent stats for the
abyss monolith. Additionally, extra
unused feathers from the faction maps
can be converted to enhancement stones
and power shards. Next up, cubes. These
are floating glimmering chests that can
be found all over the faction maps. The
red ones can only be opened if you have
a cube key, while gold ones can be
opened without anything. Although doing
so will award less items. Opening a cube
will award you with a mix of soul cexes,
rainbow soul crystals, power shards,
consumables, resurrection stones,
unstable stigma shards, gathering
materials, mana stones, kina, the
stones, odel energy, and skins. Next up,
gathering. Essence extraction is used to
gather ingredients from gathering nodes
both in the open world and in dungeons,
regardless of ingredient types. Leveling
up gathering will provide you with
common and specialty skill points which
can be used to level up passive skills
as well as improve gathering result of
certain ingredient types. Passes reduce
failure rates and increase success
efficiency with specialty points being
used to make gathering node visible on
the mini map as well as give a chance to
upgrade the amount and quality of items
received upon a successful gather. You
can only max out specialization in two
gatherables with odil being by far the
most important to level up due to the
presence of enhanced odel nodes at the
end of conquest dungeons with the
secondary choice being up to whatever
you're trying to gather. Passives and
nodes can both be respected at any point
by spending a little bit of kina and
gathering levels are character based.
Next, crafting. The crafting system is
as simplistic as it is essential and is
split in two categories. Regular
crafting and transfer crafting.
Completing a craft of any level will
award a flat amount of experience, and
earning enough experience will level up
a given craft. You start as a novice
without going up to level 50, then do a
quest to break into professional, which
also goes up to level 50 at first, going
up to level 70 in season 3. Because of
the way it works, it is possible to
simply spam the level one craft in order
to reach max level given enough crafts.
Launching a craft requires to have the
minimum level indicated next to the
craft as well as the listed ingredients.
As the craft goes, the success and fill
bar will fill up in small increments. at
rates dictated by both the grade of the
craft and level relative to the craft
with a higher level meaning a higher
chance to increase the success bar. You
can review chances of success procs by
clicking on the percent icon next to the
craft's name in the crafting menu. If
the failure bar gets to full, the craft
will be unsuccessful and ingredients
will be lost. If the success bar goes to
full, the craft will either complete and
award you with the item or will have a
percentage to proc into a high quality
item or in the case of consumables
increase the quantity crafted,
restarting the craft with a new reward.
If that happens, the craft can then go
on to fail the procked item, resulting
in ingredients being lost and no item
being awarded. You can see the chance to
proc items as well as the item it will
prog into in the crafting menu here.
Now, let's talk equipment crafting more
specifically. These follow a tiered
crafting process similar to iron one and
will be your chase item in PV. You craft
a white item that can proc into a green
version. Then use that green proc to
craft a blue item that can proc into
gold. Then use that gold item to craft
draconic equipment. Crafted Dronic
equipment are best in slot in PvE for
their given bracket providing PvE
bonuses as well as having one additional
soulbine within their tier and will be
your chase item in PVE. They will
require an artisan base which is the
proced gold pre-draconic craft as well
as draconic ingredients of different
types depending on the tier of the craft
harvested from a variety of sources with
more and more tiers of these crafts
becoming available as the game evolves.
Crafting these pieces of equipment has a
chance to fail as mentioned previously.
However, draconic equipment also has
crafting path with guaranteed success
which utilizes dragon lord cores. Dragon
lord cores can be obtained by fusing a
magical breath obtained in the season
shop alongside either the appropriate
artisan gold base or a piece of dungeon
gear corresponding with the tier and
type of the targeted craft. For example,
if you wanted to craft a dark dragon
ring through the guaranteed crafting
path, which is a tier 2 draconic craft,
you will need to merge your breath with
a tier 2 dungeon accessory, which in
this case would be an omous accessory
from the two star dungeon Rugu Canyon.
If you wanted to craft an Ebony weapon,
a tier three draconic craft, you would
need to merge your breath with a chrome
weapon from the threestar dungeon Fire
Temple, so on and so forth. Magical
breath are however limited in the amount
that can be bought each season, meaning
that you will typically use them to
secure more expensive crafts like
weapons. Do note that when crafting
items through the guaranteed success
path, the item will be bound on craft,
meaning that it will only be usable by
this character. Now, let's address
transfer crafting. The principle of that
system is basically to upgrade your
draconic piece of equipment in a
non-destructive way. Let's say, for
example, that you have a tier one
draconic ritual. Through transfer
crafting, you will be able to upgrade it
into a tier 2 draconic rate tool by
simply supplementing the missing
ingredients while retaining your
enhancement progression on it. Upon
upgrading, soul binds as well as
enhancement and amplification levels
will be kept while philosopher stone
slots and mana stones will be wiped. The
craft is also guaranteed to succeed and
can also proc. With that said, there is
a catch, which is that the item will
need to be splendid in order to upgrade
to the next tier, which is the procked
version of the item. With that said, if
your item happens to not be splendant,
you can transfer craft it into a
splendid version for a small kina fee.
Crafting levels are per character based.
Although transfer crafting does not
require crafts to be leveled up, which
means that if you want to make some
accessories for your alts, for example,
you can craft them on your main, move
them to your alt, soul bind them, then
upgrade them without having the craft
leveled up on your alt. Next, let's get
into some solo PvE content. Starting
with ascension trial. These are solo
dungeons that will have you clear rooms
of monsters, obtaining random
assortments of buffs after doing so for
the rest of the dungeon. Each time you
clear a room, then face a boss at the
end. Each room will also feature
randomly spawning crystal that will
debuff the end boss when broken. This
dungeon will be one of your main sources
of enhancement stones, also providing
unstable stigma shards, mana stones,
eyeball fragments, as well as balancina
in the form of salentium with the amount
awarded depending on the selected
difficulty as well as the clear time.
These dungeons can be done three times
per week per character. Next, nightmare
dungeons. These are solo instances that
will pit you against enhanced version of
storyline bosses. You will have a
limited amount of time to defeat the
boss and dying will reset the fight.
Bosses each have 10 levels of difficulty
and are split through three different
tiers with each tier requiring to defeat
all of the bosses of the tier below them
at level 10. Clearing nightmare bosses
will award you fantasal fragments that
can be spent in the nightmare trade
chart with the first clear of each
levels of each bosses granting
additional bonus fragments. You will be
able to select level 10 from the get-go
and clearing it will award you with all
of the fragments of the previous levels.
The nightmare trade shop features
pantheon statues of each bosses that
will be purchasable once you beat set
boss at least once regardless of its
level. The most notable statue is the
final layer boss colossus. Each season
introduces a new layer alongside a new
batch of bosses and with them their
related statues. Other notable rewards
include the skins, wings, as well as
growth items like bolt crystals and
skill points. Nightmare dungeon
allowances refresh at a rate of twice
every 24 hours and both progression and
allowances are character based. Next,
daily dungeon. Daily dungeons, a
knockdown name implies, are solo weekly
short mini gamess that currently comes
in three varieties. The first one, D.A.
I research base, will have you kill
waves of enemies and award you with
enhancement stones. The second one,
Odelium Repository, will have you kill a
boss and run around to collect colored
orbs on the ground and will award you
with pets. Finally, the third one,
Kbaki's Secret Depository, will have you
run around to pick coins while dodging
stunning bombs and will award you with
Balina. Daily dungeon allowances refresh
weekly and are server based, meaning
that you will only be running them on
one character. Next up, the meat and
bone of the game, expeditions. These are
your run-of-the-mill dungeons and will
be the bulk of your PvE activities. They
come in three different varieties:
exploration, conquest, and ordeal.
Exploration dungeons are your easy
tutorial modes. You will go through a
couple during the main story, and
opening the chest at the end will
immediately unlock the pity to make one
of the piece of equipment from that
dungeon selectable. The story dungeons
are skilled to be solable. Non-story
dungeons will also have exploration
modes with these being slightly more
difficult compared to the story ones,
requiring more players if done on level.
During these three times will also
unlock the pity to pick a piece of
equipment from those dungeons which can
be useful to bump up the power on old
characters. Conquest dungeons are your
actual endgame dungeon. They are
separated by tiers with higher tiers
giving higher level equipment and
materials and also each feature normal
and hard mode with the difference
between these being the drop rates as
well as the amount of loot earned.
Opening a chest at the end of the
dungeon will require odal energy, a
currency that recharges slowly over time
as well as is earned in a variety of
ways like in the subscriber shop or in
substance morphing. If you decide to not
open the chest at the end of the
dungeon, an unobtained cube count
allowance will be taken for a maximum of
10 dungeon runs where you do not claim
the reward per week. If you run out of
these, you will no longer be able to
enter any dungeon. This is a measure put
in place to prevent excessive carry
runs. Expeditions will award you with
kina dungeon equipment, crafting mats,
unstable stinger shards, soul by
materials, wing feather downs, painting
scraps, enhancement stones, and deon
board fragments. There is also a pity
system put in place that will award you
with rewards of your choosing after
running a dungeon a given amount of
times with rewards ranging from gear
from that specific dungeon to soul by
materials and gear exchange vouchers
that can be used to convert a piece of
equipment obtained from the dungeon into
another one of your choosing. Dungeon
rewards are personal with the equipment
being bound to your character on
acquisition. That being said, the boss
itself has a small chance to drop gear
from that dungeon as a direct ground
loot with these being tradable to other
players. Expeditions also feature a
diminishing return on the amount of kina
earned shared across the server, meaning
that playing alts in order to run more
of them for money will only be
beneficial up to a certain point. You
can view the threshold for diminishing
returns as well as your current account
by clicking on the information button
here. Next are all deals. These dungeon
types were added in chapter one and
feature juiced up version of other
expeditions on the rotation. When
running them, you will be able to put
custom affixes on them to make the
dungeon more difficult. And clearing the
dungeon will award you with subjugation
marks that can be used in the ordeal
trade shop with higher difficulty levels
awarding you more marks. The way the
mark reward works is that clearing a
level of difficulty will award you with
the marks from that level and every
levels below it, meaning that you will
really only need to do one run per week.
The trade shop features wings, crafting
materials, growth items like
amplification and soul by materials,
arcana materials, mana stones, and
resurrection spirit stones. Ordeal
requires no Odal energy to obtain
reward. Odal energy slowly refreshes
over time on a per character basis with
most of the extra sources being server
based, meaning that your main will
typically run the bulk of your weekly
dungeons. If you would like to learn
more about that, I will link a video on
old characters in the description below.
As for Odal, the shop currency
allowances reset on a per character
weekly basis. Next, transcendence
dungeons, also known as Arcana dungeons.
These are the other side of the
day-to-day endgame coin. Similarly using
odal energy to open the chest at the end
and having its own separate kina
diminishing return with the final chest
providing kina unstable sting shard theo
stones crafting mats by materials and
amplification stone fragments as well as
the unique arcana card reward but more
on these in just a bit. These dungeons
come in four difficulty levels bulking
up monsters and adding negative aixes at
each level as well as increasing the
quality of the reward. Unlike conquest
dungeons, these will also require you to
clear a certain amount of monsters
within the dungeon in order to unlock
access to the end boss. Next up,
Sanctuary. This is this game's
equivalent of a raid, requiring two
groups to tackle for a total of 10
players and basically play like high-end
dungeons, featuring one to two mini
bosses and one final boss. Each season
features one sanctuary raid with the
season 3 and chapter 1 raids having
multiple difficulty levels. Similar to
dungeons, you will need to expand Odal
energy in order to claim rewards at the
end with each raid having separate
weekly clear lockouts. Leading
Sanctuaries will award you with a large
amount of dungeon loot from the season's
dungeons, as well as a large amount of
soulbind material and kina, as well as
equipment unique to these raids, such as
special extendable weapons as well as
guards, and most importantly, equipment
slots that can only be found in these
raids. Those being bracelets in the
season 1 and season 2, sanctuary, brutes
in season 3, and seals in chapter 1.
Additionally, they similarly feature a
PD system that will allow you to claim
tickets after clearing them a certain
amount of times that can be used to
craft the raid specific equipment slot
as well as convert a weapon or guild
that you may not need into one that you
do want to use. For example, if you
obtained a great sword as a ranger, they
will allow you to convert it into a bow.
Sanctuary allowances refresh weekly on a
per character basis, and the allowance
is claimed upon killing the boss. Now,
let's have a look at PvP adjacent
content. Starting with the abyss. The
abyss has PvP permanently enabled,
meaning that you cannot flag for PvE and
will always be susceptible to being
attacked by other players. There
currently exists three abyss areas.
Lower Rashanta, which is the first abyss
area accessible at the end of the base
story line that has flying enabled.
Middle Rishanta, which was made
available in season 2 that has a higher
item level requirement and has flying
disabled, and upper Rishanta, a new
player abyss that was added in chapter 1
that can only be entered when below a
certain addable and combo power
threshold, and also limits the amount of
PVP stats you can have in it. Farming
monsters in these areas will provide
more loot than in the faction maps, as
well as unlimited kenas and special
items such as potential stones that can
be used to enhance PvP equipment. As for
both fragments and abyss points, du and
middle rashanta also features special
events such as artifact sieges and world
bosses, but more on them in just a bit.
You are alled 14 hours per area per
character per week with the ability to
add more time by using abyss time stones
that can be obtained by farming monsters
in the abyss, completing abyss quest,
substance morphing, and in the auction
house. Obtained abyss points can be
spent in the abyss shop to purchase PvP
specific equipment, medals, wings,
growth items like asphel board,
crystals, and stinger shards, as well as
consumables such as potions, and PvP
mana stones. Next up on the topic of the
abyss, abyss rifts. Abyss rifts are
special events that take place twice a
week. You can participate to them by
entering through the abyss menu when the
event is available. These pit matchmade
300 players of each faction against each
other in a flying version of metal
rashanta spawning waves of bosses all
across the map in a fixed order that
awards medals and bags containing abyss
points and enhancement stones upon being
defeated depending on your damage
contribution on a perass basis. Once
every boss has been defeated, the event
will end and every participant will be
awarded bonus abyss points and medals
with the faction that has defeated more
bosses getting a bit more. Next, arenas.
There are two types of arenas, 1v one
and 5v5. Queuing is always available and
the gear is not equalized. One v one
arenas will match you against another
player of a similar 1 v one elo. Matches
last up to 10 minutes and the first to
reach three kills win. There are two
different maps with no other objectives
than to kill the enemy player. Winning
award you with 1 v one arena elo and a
bit of a base point. 5v5 arena pit two
groups of five players against each
other and can be queued both solo and
with a pre-made. Matchmaking will
attempt to match you against the same
average elo as well as against a
pre-made. if you queue in a pre-made
yourself, but will pick whatever is
available if it cannot find a suitable
opponent. Matches last up to 10 minutes
and work like a death match where death
is permanent with the first team to
fully clear out the other team being
decided the winner. The same maps as 1 v
one arenas are used with once again no
other objectives than killing the enemy
group. Winning award you with 5v5 arena
elo and a bit of abys points. Up next,
battlegrounds. Battlegrounds pit two
forces of 10 players against each other
in a different format depending on the
season. Character progression is
equalized, maxing out every skill and
stigma levels as well as evening out
stats. Matches last up to 10 minutes
with winning conditions that varies per
format and curing times are restricted.
Participating award you with a base
points as well as medals with winning
awarding you extra of both as well as
boltable fragments. [music] Next time
events starting with rifting. Rifts
spawn every 3 hours for 10 minutes on
the main faction maps. Using the rift
will make you cross to the enemy
factions map with an allotted time of 1
hour. in case of death will send you
back to your map unless you set up a
kiss. When rifts are active, players of
opposite faction with the PVP flag
enabled will be able to attack each
other. Killing other players will award
you with abyss ranking points as well as
abyss points with a times two multiply
bonus applied if you haven't reached
your AP cap and awarding you with 10% of
the base abyss point if your cap has
been reached. Next on the topic of rift,
rift domination events. These are
special rifting events that happens six
times a week. The event will only be
active on one of the faction map at a
time, rotating which faction can be
attacked every week. To participate,
you'll need to have completed all of the
stronghold of the area as well as meet
the eye level and combat power
requirements. Then go on the map
eligible to get attacked when the event
pops up and join from the side menu.
Once the event starts, a region with
four strongholds will be picked as the
target with each strongholds being
linked to three monolith protected by
guards. Breaking all three monolith will
capture the stronghold. And if three
strongholds get captured, the attacking
faction will win. In order for the
defending faction to win, three
strongholds or more will have to be
protected until the end of the 15
minutes timer. You will be able to put
down special domination kisks to serve
as resurrection points in case of death
as the attacker with defenders only
being able to use regular kibilisks. In
the event you die with no Kisk being set
up as an attacker, you will be able to
cross back to the enemy factions map
even if the risks have closed and
clicking the space-time button on the
side menu. Although you will have to
walk all the way back to the offense
area. Participating will earn you
rewards based on overall contribution in
PvP as well as damage dealt to the
monolith, awarding boxes of medals and
AP depending on performance and with the
winners getting a bit more as well as
potential stones. Domination allowances
refresh at a rate of three per week per
server. Next, world bosses. World bosses
spawn all across the faction maps as
well as the abyss. World bosses on the
faction maps have respawn times between
1 and 12 hours with the world bosses in
the abyss either having fixed spawns on
certain days or respawning at regular
intervals. You can check the next
spawning time for world bosses in
general in the expiration tab of the
map. World bosses of the faction map
will award anyone participating with
painting scraps and boxes containing
gear that can be used in supply
deliveries with a chance to drop
Pantheon paintings and gear as ground
loot. with the world bosses in the abyss
dropping pantheon paintings and colossus
as possible ground loot as well as
awarding tokens to every participants
based on class damage contribution that
can be converted into boxes that contain
AP medals and potential stones. Do note
that only the faction that deals the
final blow will be eligible for rewards.
Next, sugar games. Sugar games open for
3 minutes at the top of every hour.
These feature mini games that pit you
against other players with a variety of
objectives. Participating to these will
award you with a base point and painting
scraps, consumables, crafting materials,
as well as tokens that can be spent in
the festival shop in varying quantities
depending on your performance. Notable
items in the festival shop include skill
points, div and ball crystals, wings,
pets, as well as skins. Games can be
played as much as you want, but the
rewards can only be claimed with
allowances that refresh at a rate of two
allowances per day per server. Next,
invasions. These open every 2 hours at
halfass for 3 minutes. These function in
a similar fashion as sugar games, except
you will have to defeat waves of enemies
as well as a boss. Rewards are the same
as sugar games and are also based on
performance. Although the threshold for
max contribution is very low, these
refresh at a rate of one allowance per
day per server. Next, artifact sieges.
Artifact sieges happen twice a week at a
fixed timing with the next schedule
siege being visible in the abyss menu.
They take place in lower rashanta as
well as middle Rashanta with each having
three artifacts to be captured. A boss
will spawn on each artifact and the
faction that deals the final blow to say
boss will gain control of that artifact
until next siege. Victors of the
artifact will be awarded medals and
abyss points based on overall PvP and
PvE contributions. Additionally, each
artifacts claimed by the faction will
provide a small boost to abyss points
earned within the area, become a
teleport point, as well as access to a
special solo instance called abyss
corridor. You will be able to enter the
abyss corridors by clicking on the rift
present on top of the conquered
artifact. Entering an abyssal corridor
will teleport you to a solo instance
with fast respawning trash monsters that
give you a sizable amount of AP when
killed for a duration of 2 minutes and
10 seconds. Corridor allowances are
character based and can only be entered
once per artifact per victory. Next,
progression systems. Starting with
achievements. Achievements are earned by
doing a wide range of activities in
game. Most will award you with a bit of
kina, but some will give you valuable
items like pantheon decorations or
titles. Achievement progression is
character based. Next, title. Idols are
earned in a variety of ways, whether
through rank rewards, quests, or
achievements. Some are purely cosmetic,
but most will provide you with both
passives and active stats. Passive stats
will permanently be added to your
character upon obtaining an achievement,
making it so you will eventually want to
hunt all of them. Active stats vary by
achievement types with there being three
types: offensive, defensive, and
special, and will only be active if you
select that title to be equipped. With
that said, you can toggle titles to be
equipped only for the title or only for
